text:
New Jersey arrives with three straight wins, the latest a 3-1 beat-down of Los Angeles, and a record that undersells them: the Devils have taken 60% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) this season, but finishing and goaltending have cost them. Dallas comes in on a five-game winning streak, the latest a 6-3 win over the Islanders, and is playing without Oskar Bäck and Esa Lindell. Sam Steel is day-to-day and could return.

The Devils lead on chance creation (3.67 expected goals per 60 minutes against 3.10), though Dallas has allowed fewer goals per game (1.73 to 2.91). Special teams are close: the power plays are even at 0.74 and 0.75 expected goals per game. The Stars take 4.1 penalties a game, which keeps handing opponents power plays. In net, projected starter Jake Oettinger is 9.3 goals saved above expected (how many goals he's stopped beyond what the shots should allow) this season, while projected New Jersey starter Jake Allen sits at -3.1. Our model has it nearly even: 2.92 expected goals for New Jersey, 2.83 for Dallas.

Watch Arseny Gritsyuk, who has scored in five straight games; as Mike Fink of The Hockey News posted, "It's Gritsyuk's fifth goal in as many games." He has a 19% chance to score tonight, though we'd expect some cooling. Jack Hughes is our top pick on the New Jersey side at 31%, and Anthony Mantha plays his 600th NHL game. For Dallas, Wyatt Johnston (37%) and Jason Robertson (36%) lead the way.
